disease_label_per_paper: Hypocomplementemic urticarial vasculitis syndrome with severe renal and gastrointestinal involvement
presentation_summary: 56-year-old man was referred with fever, abdominal pain, laboratory inflammation, and impaired kidney function.
HUVS had been suspected years earlier after wheals and arthralgia; prior skin histology primarily showed urticaria but early leukocytoclastic vasculitis could not be excluded.
Current examination showed tender abdomen and urticarial-like lesions on upper arms and thighs.
Laboratory workup showed CRP 55 mg/L, creatinine 389 µmol/L, tubular proteinuria, microhematuria, acanthocytes, granular casts, low C3, low C4, and anti-C1q 171 U/mL.
Kidney biopsy showed severe chronic tubulointerstitial injury and small-artery fibrinoid necrosis compatible with renal vasculitic involvement.
CT lungs showed crazy-paving patterns with diffuse ground-glass opacities in both lower lobes.

Persistent severe abdominal pain progressed to ischemic colonic lesions, sepsis with peritonitis signs, emergent laparotomy, and subtotal colectomy; colon histology showed acute necrotizing vasculitis of submucosal vessels and fibrin thrombi.
Treatment included prednisolone plus mycophenolate, then cyclophosphamide, then rituximab maintenance; renal function partially recovered at 13 months.

imaging.finding: Crazy-paving patterns with diffuse ground-glass opacities in both lower lobes.
imaging.source_text_value: Computed tomography (CT) of the lungs showed crazy-paving patterns with diffuse ground-glass opacities in both lower lobes

imaging.finding: No clear large- or medium-vessel occlusion despite ischemic colonic lesions.
imaging.source_text_value: no clear occlusions of large or medium-sized vessels were evident on abdominal CT angiography

imaging.finding: Global hypokinesia, LVEF 40%, and left ventricular thrombus; cardiac MRI two weeks later showed no active inflammation.
imaging.source_text_value: cardiac ultrasound revealed global hypokinesia with reduced LVEF of 40% and left ventricular thrombus; cardiac MRI showed no active inflammation

biopsy.finding: Diffuse interstitial fibrosis/tubular atrophy, tubulointerstitial inflammation and tubulitis, acute tubulointerstitial injury, and small-artery fibrinoid necrosis.
biopsy.source_text_value: features of vasculitis, e.g., fibrinoid necrosis of small arteries, were seen

biopsy.finding: Acute necrotizing vasculitis of submucosal vessels with fibrinoid necrosis and fresh intravascular fibrin thrombi.
biopsy.source_text_value: Light microscopy of the resected colon showed acute necrotizing vasculitis of submucosal vessels, i.e., fibrinoid necrosis, alongside fresh intravascular fibrin-thrombi.

diagnostics.source_text_value: ANA, ANCA, cryoglobulins, rheumatoid factors, antiphospholipid antibodies, anti-dsDNA, anti-Sm, anti-SS-A, anti-SS-B and multiple others were negative except elevated anti-C1q, anti-histone, and anti-chromatin
HIV and hepatitis B virus serology tests were negative. Hepatitis C virus RNA was not detected.
no affections of the eyes were found

clinical_course.event: Prednisolone 50 mg/day and mycophenolate mofetil 1000 mg/day were initiated after HUVS diagnosis was confirmed.
clinical_course.source_text_value: Immunosuppressive therapy using oral prednisolone 50 mg/day and mycophenolate mofetil 1000 mg/day was initiated.

clinical_course.event: Severe abdominal pain progressed to colonic ischemia, sepsis with peritonitis signs, and subtotal colectomy.
clinical_course.source_text_value: patient became septic with guarding and rebound tenderness... almost the entire colon was found to be ischemic; thus, subtotal colectomy with terminal ileostomy was necessary

clinical_course.event: Cyclophosphamide was given after severe GI vasculitis, followed by rituximab maintenance.
clinical_course.source_text_value: immunosuppressive therapy was intensified with cyclophosphamide 15 mg/kg initially and 10 mg/kg three weeks later... maintenance therapy with rituximab

clinical_course.event: At 13 months, renal function partially recovered; delayed rituximab was followed by arthralgia that resolved after rituximab.

confirmatory_findings.finding: Schwartz criteria met by recurrent urticarial exanthema, hypocomplementemia, abdominal pain, arthralgia, and positive anti-C1q

quality_warnings: This is organ-threatening HUVS with current GI and renal disease; infection/sepsis during the course is preserved as a complication and not used to erase UV evidence.
Cocaine exposure is stored as a GI ischemia modifier, not as a disease-name qualifier.
Biopsy and colectomy pathology are post-workup evidence; presentation evidence retains fever, rash, abdominal pain, renal labs, complement, and anti-C1q.
